entries.subject: Radius
entries.finding: 1.1 Jupiter radii from the NASA Exoplanet Archive's calculated radius (its Chen & Kipping 2017 mass-radius relationship): a model, not a measurement, since HD 118203 c does not transit, via the NASA Exoplanet Archive.

entries.subject: Mass
entries.finding: 11.79 Jupiter masses: Zhang et al. 2024, the mass the NASA Exoplanet Archive's composite table adopts (2024AJ....168..295Z), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024AJ....168..295Z/abstract).

entries.subject: Orbit
entries.finding: Zhang et al. 2024 (2024AJ....168..295Z), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname ZHANG_ET_AL__2024): P 5103 d; Zhang et al. 2024 (2024AJ....168..295Z), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname ZHANG_ET_AL__2024): a/R* derived from its semi-major axis 6.28 au and stellar radius 2.04 solar radii; inclination 93.7 +11.9 degrees, measured in the same fit; Zhang et al. 2024 (2024AJ....168..295Z), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname ZHANG_ET_AL__2024): e 0.26; Zhang et al. 2024 (2024AJ....168..295Z), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname ZHANG_ET_AL__2024): omega 175 degrees; Zhang et al. 2024 (2024AJ....168..295Z), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname ZHANG_ET_AL__2024): periastron passage 2452527 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; Display convention: the NASA Exoplanet Archive carries no position angle for the orbit's node on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north)..
